item.title: Auditors: €9.5bn needed to put roads and railways on war footing
item.description:
Auditors: €9.5bn needed to put roads and railways on war footing

October 14, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The Netherlands needs to invest nearly €10 billion to make its road and rail infrastructure fit for war, auditors have warned in a critical report.

The Court of Audit said investment was needed to upgrade motorways and rail lines to ensure military vehicles and supplies can be transported across the country.

“Shortfalls in the maintenance budget mean that on an everyday basis, infrastructure is so outdated that it can no longer be used properly,” the auditors said.

“This leads to limitations on use, such as traffic travelling at lower speeds or with lighter loads, which military transport also has to contend with.”

The Netherlands’ key strategic position on the edge of the North Sea makes it a crucial link in the chain for military supplies to Nato partners. A broken bridge or subsidence on the railway line could have far-reaching consequences, the auditors warned.

Last year junior infrastructure minister Thierry Aartsen called for a review of the railway lines between the Netherlands and the Baltic states, after researchers warned that the network was prone to sabotage.

Railway sabotage

A month ago saboteurs brought the network to a standstill by fastening steel pipes and other objects to rail lines, in a co-ordinated campaign that was blamed on farmers angry with the government’s plans to tackle the nitrogen emissions crisis.

Altogether the audit office says the country needs to spend an extra €9.5bn, including €5 billion to meet Nato standards by widening military corridors, raising clearance heights and strengthening bridges.

They added that the list was incomplete because it does not include spending on waterways or how much was needed to maintain military corridors in their current state.

The figure is far greater than the €1.5bn the cabinet announced in its 2027 budget for repairs to roads and bridges over the next decade. All Nato countries agreed at last year’s summit in The Hague to raise defence spending to 5% of GDP, including 1.5% on critical infrastructure.

item.title: ASML posts record quarter as AI demand outpaces expansion plans
item.description:
ASML posts record quarter as AI demand outpaces expansion plans

October 14, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Dutch chip-machine maker ASML had a record third quarter, with sales of €11.7 billion and net profit of €5 billion. That is well up from the €2.1 billion profit last year.

ASML is benefiting from the boom in AI, with customers continuously raising their forecasts for how many machines they will need.

That puts pressure on ASML to make more machines. The company had planned to raise capacity by 30% in 2027, with a possible further 30% in 2028, but now says even that will not fully meet customer demand.

Sales of upgrades for existing machines also rose above expectations, reaching €3.3 billion, helping push the profit margin to 57.5%.

ASML expects fourth-quarter sales of between €14.2 billion and €15.2 billion, and between €44 billion and €45 billion for the full year. Shareholders will receive an interim dividend of €1.88 per share in November.

item.title: VeiligThuis denied plea for extra funding for domestic abuse
item.description:
VeiligThuis denied plea for extra funding for domestic abuse

October 14, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Domestic abuse reporting network VeiligThuis had its request for an additional
€70 million rejected by parliament on Tuesday, after the organisation said it was being overwhelmed with reports and could not handle the workload.

Waiting lists have been growing substantially for years, and how a case is handled depends on the region where you live.

MPs voted against immediately granting more money. First, parliament wants the cabinet to look at the “role, position and capacity” of VeiligThuis to see how best to improve it. A motion calling for that investigation was passed a year ago.

MPs agreed the motion needs to be implemented now, but that more money is not the solution until the problems are better understood.

Pro MP Lisa Westerveld said the previous and current cabinets are responsible for the delay. “This is not primarily a matter of money, but of doing what was promised.”

In the past year, serious child abuse incidents have sparked national outrage and drawn attention to the lack of sufficient resources and care.

item.title: Senate votes to axe penalty payments for asylum applicants
item.description:
Senate votes to axe penalty payments for asylum applicants

October 14, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Senators voted on Tuesday to scrap all penalty payments to asylum seekers whose applications are delayed beyond the legal six month deadline.

This means that anyone applying for asylum status in the Netherlands and has to wait more than the maximum term of 6 months for a decision, will not be financially compensated for having to wait longer than promised.

The decision was agreed with a large majority; asylum minister Bart van den Brink announced recently that the immigration service IND had paid out almost €100 million in penalties for missing deadlines in the first seven months of 2026.

The IND said penalty payments do nothing to speed up decisions.

The legal changes agreed in the senate also introduce rules allowing authorities to detain people who are deliberately refusing or avoiding leaving the country despite having an application rejected. It also makes it easier to declare foreign nationals convicted of crimes “undesirable”.

The changes do not include another idea, first proposed by the right-wing PVV, which would formally criminalise illegal residence. This caused controversy in April when it was voted down, as it could mean anyone without their residency paperwork sorted out (including foreign nationals whose permits lapsed) could be prosecuted.

D66 senator Boris Dittrich told Dutch News at the time that the law, if passed, could open the door to a future right-wing cabinet “hunt down all illegal immigrants.”

Van den Brink has since proposed a narrower bill that would only criminalise rejected asylum seekers who actively “frustrate” their return, with a maximum penalty of six months in jail.

item.title: Alkmaar moves protest against Israeli fans amid safety concerns
item.description:
Alkmaar moves protest against Israeli fans amid safety concerns

October 14, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The mayor of Alkmaar, Anja Schouten, has ordered two demonstrations against Thursday’s Europa League match between AZ and Hapoel Be’er Sheva to be moved away from the stadium because of concerns about potential disorder.

Hundreds of people are expected to attend the protests against the participation of Israeli clubs in European competition, which have been organised by pro-Palestinian groups Boycott 4 Palestine and Week 4 Palestine.

The protests were originally due to take place outside the main entrance to the AFAS Stadium, but Schouten ordered the demonstrators to gather near the Kooimeer roundabout, the main road junction leading to the stadium, instead.

“It is not possible to take adequate management measures to prevent disorder and separate fans going to the stadium from demonstrators,” Schouten said.

“This [new] location allows us to facilitate the safe arrival and departure of demonstrators. We also need to prevent confrontations taking place with other groups.”

 

View this post on Instagram

 

A post shared by Week.4PalestineNL (@week.4palestinenl)

In a briefing note to councillors, the mayor said there were indications that supporters of the Israeli club were planning to travel to Alkmaar in spite of the ban.

“There are fears that protesters will come into conflict with each other, with supporters’ groups or with the police, that vandalism could ensue, or that the safety of people attending the match could be endangered,” she wrote.

Schouten came under fire from opposition parties on the city council last week for her decision to ban Israeli supporters from travelling to the match. AZ Alkmaar cancelled ticket sales to visiting fans in the wake of the mayor’s decision.

Amsterdam riots

She said the decision was based on public order concerns rather than “political considerations”, following the riots surrounding a Europa League game between Ajax and Maccabi Tel Aviv in Amsterdam two years ago.

Schouten said it was “virtually impossible” to keep groups apart outside the stadium, especially as many visiting fans were expected to stay in Amsterdam for the game.

Alkmaar had originally said Israeli supporters were welcome at the game, but the mayor changed her mind after her counterpart in Amsterdam, Femke Halsema, made an “urgent” appeal not to allow a repeat of the scenes in the capital in 2024.

VVD councillor John van der Rhee accused Schouten of succumbing to a “powerplay” by the mayor of Amsterdam.

item.title: PSV punished for missed chances as Leipzig claim narrow CL win
item.description:
PSV punished for missed chances as Leipzig claim narrow CL win

October 14, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Peter Bosz was left ruing missed chances after his PSV team lost 1-0 in Leipzig to move down the Champions League table.

Ivan Perisic missed a penalty in the 18th minute during a bright start for the visitors, after RB Leipzig defender Ridle Baku was penalised for handball.

But in the second period PSV were on the back foot and Brajan Gruda fired in the winner in the 75th minute with a shot that took a deflection off the luckless Perisic’s back.

“I thought we were the better team for a lot of this match,” Bosz told Ziggo Sport afterwards. “The first 30 to 35 minutes were all us, but towards half-time we started to struggle.

“Leipzig had some big chances but so did we. We played a settled game and could keep the ball for longer.”

Brazilian defender Mauro Junior also said his team deserved more from the game. “We created enough chances, but at this level you have to take them,” he said.

The result extends a winless run for PSV in Germany dating back nearly 50 years to 1977, when they beat Eintracht Braunschweig 2-1. Since then they have lost 14 matches and drawn three, against Bayern Munich in 1986, Werder Bremen in 1995 and Bayer Leverkusen last year.

It also leaves PSV in 25th place out of the 36 teams in the Champions League table, with five of those below them still to play their second-round matches. Those teams include Feyenoord, who take on Italian club Como in Rotterdam on Wednesday evening.

Next week PSV face another tricky test away to Portuguese champions Porto, coached by former Ajax manager Francesco Farioli.

item.title: Weekly regional transport strikes begin, to run until Christmas
item.description:
Weekly regional transport strikes begin, to run until Christmas

October 14, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Regional bus and train services across most of the country are disrupted by strikes as of Wednesday morning, which trade unions CNV and FNV organised over pay and working conditions.

Staff at regional operators Arriva, EBS, Qbuzz, Transdev and Keolis are taking part. National rail operator NS is running a normal service.

City transport in Amsterdam and The Hague, run by GVB and HTM, is not affected because it falls outside the regional pay deal. In Rotterdam, RET trams and metro trains are running but its buses are not. Few or no buses and trams are expected to run in Utrecht.

The strikes could continue every week until Christmas unless the unions’ demands are met. They want higher wages, quicker access to permanent contracts for staff, and better working schemes for older employees.

They will announce each week’s strike day only shortly beforehand, assuming their demands aren’t met. They also plan to pick a different day each week, so operators can’t prepare emergency timetables and the same passengers are not hit every week.

item.title: Woman, 29, goes missing in Amsterdam on bike with unknown man
item.description:
Woman, 29, goes missing in Amsterdam on bike with unknown man

October 13, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Police say they are concerned for the safety of a woman who went missing in Amsterdam after she was seen cycling with an unknown man more than a week ago.

Hajar, 29, left the Rai area in the direction of Buitenveldert last Sunday, October 4. Police said she and the man were riding a black ladies’ bike.

She is described as between 1.65m and 1.70m tall with dark curly hair and dark eyes. The day before she went missing she was wearing a tiger print dress and white New Balance shoes, but it is not clear if she was still wearing the same outfit when she left Rai.

“The police and Hajar’s family are concerned about her welfare,” a police spokesman said.

item.title: Dutch-born panda cub Lang Yue to move to China this month
item.description:
Dutch-born panda cub Lang Yue to move to China this month

October 13, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Lang Yue, the giant panda cub born at Ouwehands Dierenpark in Rhenen, Utrecht, two years ago, will leave for China at the end of October, the zoo has said.

The zoo agreed with the China Wildlife Conservation Association that giant pandas born outside China must move there before their fourth birthday, the zoo said in a statement.

Lang Yue, who was born on July 12, 2024, no longer depends on her mother for food. In the wild, giant panda cubs stay with their mother for about two years before living alone.

In China she will join the national breeding programme for the species, and the zoo hopes she will eventually have cubs of her own. Ouwehands zoo is also planning a farewell ceremony.

Her parents, Wu Wen and Xing Ya, will stay in Rhenen. They arrived from China in 2017 as part of a conservation partnership between the zoo and China, broadcaster NOS reported. The zoo is hoping the pair will breed again.

Lang Yue is the second panda born in the Netherlands. Her older sister Fan Xing, born in May 2020, was sent to China in September 2023.

item.title: Albert Heijn begins restocking as hack traced to foreign servers
item.description:
Albert Heijn begins restocking as hack traced to foreign servers

October 13, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Albert Heijn has started restocking its supermarkets and restarting some IT systems, two days after a “cyber incident” took down many of its supply chains.

Parent company Ahold Delhaize said on Tuesday it was carrying out a “controlled restart of certain systems” and had so far found no indication that customer data had been stolen. It has not said which systems are back up.

Sources in the security sector told broadcaster NOS that Albert Heijn had identified suspicious attack traffic on its systems. According to NOS, the chain’s security staff appear to have switched systems off as the traffic came in, preventing the hackers from getting deeper into the network.

Foreign servers
The company knows that several servers were used in the attack, in the US, Poland, Moldova and Turkey, the sources said. The location of a server doesn’t mean that that is where the attacks are coming from, as traffic can be routed through other countries.

Albert Heijn’s investigation also suggests that servers belonging to Ahold Delhaize’s US arm may be involved. “That could mean the hackers broke into those servers and used them to attack Dutch systems,” cybersecurity expert Pim Takkenberg told NOS.

Another expert, Joey Fennis, said hackers were clearly involved, but it was not yet possible to say what, if any, damage it had caused. “It may also be that Albert Heijn detected them in time,” he said.

Albert Heijn said in a written statement that it was taking the incident “very seriously”, but could not go into technical details at this point.

Shop impacts 
Work at some of Albert Heijn’s six distribution centres in the Netherlands stopped completely on Monday, leaving gaps on shelves. The chain now says several centres are operating, and it is laying on extra deliveries.

Albert Heijn says some shelves may stay empty, like fruit, vegetables and other fresh produce. Online ordering and deliveries are still not possible, and customer service is still unreachable. Chemist chain Etos and off-licence chain Gall & Gall are also affected.

Other countries 
Belgian supermarket chain Delhaize, also owned by Ahold Delhaize, reported IT problems on Monday. Albert Heijn’s stores in Belgium are supplied from the Tilburg distribution centre, and the chain told broadcaster VRT the impact there was limited.

The incident came on the same weekend as a separate cyberattack on hundreds of supermarkets in France. There, hackers remotely forced refrigeration systems to defrost, and chains including Intermarché and Coopérative U had to throw away fresh and frozen food.

An Ahold Delhaize spokesperson told news agency Reuters there was no evidence of a link between the two attacks.
